title: Model drift signal strategy and dashboard sketches
summary: Working notes for building a pragmatic, cost-aware model-drift observability surface: metric candidates, tracing attachments, adaptive sampling, and dashboard wireframes for per-model / per-tenant drift detection and investigation.
content:
Problem statement:
We need observability that reliably surfaces (and makes actionable) two classes of drift: (1) feature/input drift (distributional changes of incoming requests) and (2) model-output drift (changes in model behavior relative to expected labels or quality proxies). Goal is low-noise alerts, cheap sampling for human review, and fast investigator workflows that link traces, prompts, and recent model rollouts.

Guiding principles (pragmatic / production-first):
- Signal first: prefer a small set of high-signal metrics per tenant/model rather than many noisy indicators.
- Cost-aware sampling: trace and label budget are limited — implement prioritized sampling (high-risk tenants/model routes get more labels/traces).
- Actionability: every alert should include an investigation starter (recent prompt examples, embedding cluster shifts, representative failed outputs).
- Rollout-aware: attribute drift to model version, prompt template change, or upstream schema change when possible.

High-level architecture sketch:
- Ingest metrics: per-request features (hashed), model outputs (token stats, probabilities, embeddings), routing metadata (model id, model version, tenant id, route), and rollout tags.
- Short-term store: 7-14 day high-cardinality buffer for real-time drift detection.
- Long-term aggregate store: 90+ day rolling aggregates for baseline comparisons.
- Sampling controller: policy engine that decides which requests to persist full trace / enqueue for human labeling.

Metric candidates and concise definitions (candidate list — pick ~6 for pilot):
1) input-embedding-shift: median cosine distance between recent input embeddings and baseline window (baseline = 30d historical sample).
   - unit: median cosine distance (0..2)
   - signal: slow increase or sudden jump indicates new kinds of prompts
2) output-logprob-drop: change in mean token log-probability conditioned on same prompt distribution (proxy for confidence/drop in fluency).
   - unit: delta mean token logprob
3) answer-distribution-kld: KL divergence between categorical top-choices distribution (e.g., classification outputs or binned semantics) over baseline window.
   - unit: nats (KL)
4) perplexity-shift: relative change in perplexity under a reference model (small language model trained on expected outputs) for recent outputs.
   - unit: multiplicative ratio or percent change
5) hallucination-proxy-rate: fraction of outputs that trigger heuristic hallucination detectors (e.g., unsupported-entity-rate, contradictions with context).
   - unit: percentage of requests
6) replay-failure-rate: fraction of sampled prompts where replay against pinned model version changed output substantially (used to surface regression-per-tenant).
   - unit: percentage

Operational thresholds: keep conservative alerting for initial rollout — e.g., 3-sigma sustained for 6 hours for tenants >X qps, 12 hours for lower volume tenants. Use two-tier alerting: soft alert (notified to owners, lower noise) and hard alert (page on-call when both signal and sampling-confirmed label anomalies).

Sampling plan (budget-aware):
- Tier buckets per tenant by monthly tokens: Platinum (>1T tokens), Gold (100B-1T), Silver (<100B). Higher tiers get more labeling/tracing budget.
- Prioritized sampling criteria (ordered): sudden embedding shift, high output-logprob-drop, recent model rollouts, unusual route change. Each criterion assigns a priority score; sampling budget consumed by descending score.
- Reservoir quotas: maintain per-tenant per-day quotas to avoid one tenant consuming full labeling budget.
- Label routing: sampled items get routed to: a) quick automated heuristics (fast label), b) human label queue, c) replay jobs (re-run under previous model versions).

Tracing notes (how to tie traces to drift investigation):
- Span enrichment: attach model_id, model_version, rollout_tag, tenant_id, prompt_hash, input_embedding_id, sampling_priority, and sampling_reason to the root span.
- Breadcrumbs: capture last N tokens of prompt (redacted) and first 200 chars of output as attributes to speed triage.
- Trace sampling policy: dynamic sampling multiplier when metric deviation > threshold to capture more full traces for debugging.
- Privacy: redact PII from captured traces; store hashes/embeddings rather than raw sensitive text when required by tenant policy.

Dashboard wireframes — investigation-first (notes, not final UI):
Frame A: Model Health Overview (top row)
- Small tiles per model: embedding-shift (sparklines), perplexity-ratio, hallucination-proxy-rate, replay-failure-rate. Click model => tenant breakdown.
- Global timeline with colored bands for model rollouts / config changes.

Frame B: Tenant Drift Lane (per-tenant, left-to-right investigation flow)
- Left column: traffic summary (qps, token-rate, dominant routes).
- Middle: anomaly timeline (stacked signals with hover examples).
- Right: sample bank (prioritized sampled prompts, human labels, replays) with quick actions: mark false-positive, create bug, pin example to dashboard.

Frame C: Embedding space explorer
- UMAP t-SNE sketch of recent vs baseline embeddings with cluster change highlights. Select cluster -> list of examples, model outputs, and associated traces.

Frame D: Rollout attribution view
- Compare metric deltas around rollout windows; show per-version deltas and percent of tenants affected. Include quick link to rollback button (gated).

Investigation playbook (operator steps):
1) See soft alert for tenant X: open Tenant Drift Lane.
2) Check small-sample examples in sample bank; if automated heuristics mark >50% as problematic, escalate.
3) Run replay on representative prompts against pinned previous model. If divergence, create regression ticket and attach traces + sample set.
4) If input-embedding-shift but outputs stable, open question to Product for expected prompt distribution change; downgrade alert if intentional.

Labeling taxonomy (short):
- OK: output acceptable against spec
- Degraded: reduced quality but not harmful
- Hallucination: unsupported assertion or fabricated entity
- Safety: harmful content
- Intent-change: user intent not in scope (feature request vs bug)

Alert lifecycle & ownership:
- Soft alerts: sent to model owners + tenant owners, include sample bank, no paging. Auto-resolve when metrics back within baseline for 24h.
- Hard alerts: paging to on-call SRE only if high-impact tenant OR cross-tenant widespread drift (>5% tenants show signal) AND sampling confirms >30% problematic outputs.

Mini experiments to run during pilot (3-week sprints):
- Week 1: Probe embedding-shift metric sensitivity with synthetic perturbations (prefix insertion, language shift).
- Week 2: Deploy prioritized sampler; measure label budget consumption and sample utility (how many samples are true positives).
- Week 3: Build minimal dashboard with model tiles + sample bank and run tabletop incident for drift.

Open questions / risks:
- Baseline selection: rolling 30d window may include slowly drifting baseline; consider multi-horizon baselines (7d, 30d, 90d) and weight recent more.
- Multi-tenant noise: small tenants produce few samples — need to borrow statistical power across similar tenants/routes.
- Cost of embedding retention: storing high-cardinality embeddings for many tenants is expensive; consider hashed sketches or centroid-based retention for low-tier tenants.

Action items (owners):
- (Anya) finalize metric formulas and wire them up to ingestion schema (deadline 2025-10-17).
- (Lucas) prototype prioritized sampler and reservoir quotas (deadline 2025-10-24).
- (Marta) design 2-page dashboard mock in Figma and handoff to frontend (deadline 2025-10-31).
- (Ibrahim) draft privacy redaction checklist and tenant opt-out flow (deadline 2025-10-20).

References and helpers:
- Synthetic probe scripts: github.com/redwood-inference/obs-probes (PR linked above).
- Confluence: OBS-DRIFT-1 -- longer product writeup and acceptance criteria.

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep initial alerts conservative. We can expand later to per-route micro-alerts once signal maturity is high.
- Consider experimenting with contrastive embedding metrics (distance to minority clusters) rather than only global medians.
